Unit: rad on rotary axes, m on linear axes; floored per axis by gear to counts. Allowed: finite >0 and at least one count on every axis. Default: required inside drive_supervision. drive_supervision_doc: Unverified example. Unit: machine-level object applied identically to every axis. Allowed: the three annotated fields; per-axis declarations do not exist. Home acquisition stationarity is joint_unit_tolerances.hold_displacement_tolerance_rad, not a supervision field. Default: omitted, which disables the enable, brake-release and disarm-motion supervision (configuration identity unchanged). Prevents per-joint supervision numbers and source-code defaults for drive-specific bounds.

tracking_lag_allowance.lag_allowance_ms_doc: Unverified example (a Rosie 1430 arm's value: owner's chosen margin over the ~27 ms command-to-feedback lag measured on a Rosie 1430 arm's stop dumps 2026-10-06; issue #158). Unit: ms of servo lag behind the commanded target. Allowed: integer 1..1000 (1000 is an unverified sanity cap), one value for every axis. Default: required inside tracking_lag_allowance. Prevents the lag a loaded arm shows at speed (error = |commanded velocity| x lag) tripping the static target-lead warning and following-error fault during ordinary fast motion.

jog_jerk.jerk_rad_s3_doc: Unverified example (a Rosie 1430 arm's value: sized so the smoothing window, 2 x 4*pi rad/s^2 / 150 rad/s^3 = 168 ms at 1 kHz, spans one period of the ~5.9 Hz J4 ringing seen after jog starts/stops on the 2026-10-06 stop dump; issue #158). Unit: rad/s^3 at the joint. Allowed: integer 1..100000 (100000 is an unverified sanity cap), one value for every axis; every axis must be rotary. Default: required inside jog_jerk. Prevents the one-cycle acceleration steps of the acceleration-limited jog integrator at every jog start, EndJog, input expiry and Halt ramp.

jog_jerk_doc: Unverified example. Unit: machine-level object applied identically to every axis. Prevents per-joint jerk numbers and the one-cycle acceleration steps that excite arm resonances at jog starts and stops. Allowed: jerk_rad_s3 only; per-axis declarations are refused. rtctl sizes one smoothing window N = ceil(2 x a_max / jerk / cycle) cycles from the largest jog_acceleration or max_acceleration of any axis (at most 1024 cycles, at least 2) and emits jog_jerk=<jerk>|<N> on every axis. Natively the commanded jog/Halt target is the mean of the acceleration-limited integrator's last N positions: acceleration stays within each axis's own limit and jerk within the configured value for any input, reversals included; outputs never pass a position limit the integrator respects. Stops take N cycles longer and travel |v| x N x cycle / 2 further. Planned trajectories are never smoothed natively; OLP Move-to and Cartesian steps bound their own jerk by this same value, read from the digest-bound compile (rtctl Compiled.JogJerk). Not part of the public Describe schema. Default: omitted, which keeps the unsmoothed acceleration-limited jog (configuration identity unchanged).
verify_parameter_storage_doc: Unverified example. Unit: boolean, one machine-level choice for every axis. Allowed: true only when every axis's drive tuning catalog declares parameter_storage (A6-EC: C13.10 0x2013:11, store 1, RAM-only 0). Default: false; rt-core neither reads nor writes the storage mode (configuration identity unchanged). When true, every axis gets that object as its first startup descriptor at the store value: rt-core reads it in PREOP, writes it only when it differs, and startup readback gates config_verified_mask on it. Required by startup_trial; keep it on after the last trial ends, since a RAM-only window may leave the stored mode off. Prevents a drive that silently stopped storing SDO writes (and with it the HM35 Home offset 607C) going unnoticed.
tracking_lag_allowance_doc: Unverified example. Unit: machine-level object applied identically to every axis. Allowed: lag_allowance_ms only; per-axis declarations are refused. Natively each axis's target-lead and following-error bound becomes its static limits value plus |commanded velocity| x lag_allowance_ms in that axis's own units, so no per-joint or gear-specific number exists; following_error_timeout_ms is unchanged and following error stays a fault. Not part of the public Describe schema. Default: omitted, which keeps the static bounds (configuration identity unchanged). Prevents per-joint tracking numbers and widened static bounds that would also loosen the stationary tracking check.
drive_speed_limit_motor_rpm_doc: Standalone flat/no-URDF fixture only. Unit: motor rpm. Allowed: finite >0; A6 motor frame at most 6000. Default: 3000 for fixtures; forbidden on URDF-mapped robots, whose per-axis drive cap derives from URDF velocity and robot gearing. Prevents a second independent robot speed limit.
drive_speed_limit_motor_rpm_source: Owner decision 2026-09-15: A6M rated speed 3000 rpm, spec sheet and A6M60-400H2B1-M17 / A6M80-1000H2B1-M17 part numbers. One motor revolution is 131072 counts in the drive frame regardless of the electronic gear ratio, so a motor speed cap does not scale with the gear: 0x607F counts/s = drive_speed_limit_motor_rpm / 60 * motor_encoder_counts_per_rev. Independent of the inhibited start-up verification speed bound and software limits.max_velocity.

startup.a6ec_load_inertia_ratio_doc: Unverified example of a drive tuning-catalog key (config/drives/a6ec.tuning.json, C00.06 0x2000:07). Unit: the catalog's raw drive unit (percent here), or {"value": x, "unit": "<catalog unit>"} where x / scale must be whole. Allowed: every read_write catalog key for the axis's drive, within its catalog min..max and allowed values; class tuning keys may differ between axes, class uniform keys must be one value on every axis. Default: omitted; no write, the drive keeps whatever it holds. Prevents a servo tuning value living only in the drive's EEPROM, outside every configuration identity.

axes.startup_doc: Unverified example. Unit: JSON object. Allowed: the annotated fields below, with mutually exclusive branches selected before compilation. Default: omitted; the feature is not selected. Prevents silently inventing startup settings.
axes.startup_trial_doc: Unverified example. Unit: list of this axis's startup keys. Allowed: distinct drive tuning-catalog keys this axis writes in startup (never gearing, direction or tracking mode); requires verify_parameter_storage. Default: omitted; every startup value is stored by the drive. A listed value that differs from what the drive holds is written between storage off and storage on (A6-EC C13.10 = 0, writes, C13.10 = 1), so it lives in drive RAM: a drive power cycle reverts it to the stored value, rt-core writes it again at its next start, and until then startup readback refuses configuration verification. Journal 'WARNING: startup_trial ...' and status storage=ram_only mark it. Finalize by removing the key from this list; the drive stores it at the first start that reads a different value (after a drive power cycle). Prevents commissioning trials wearing drive EEPROM (ALF1.3) and surviving as the drive's stored value.
axes.observe_doc: Unverified example. Unit: list of drive tuning-catalog keys. Allowed: 1..64 distinct catalog keys of the axis's drive, none also written in startup on that axis. Default: the machine-level observe list when the machine declares one (an axis list replaces it for that axis); otherwise nothing is observed. rt-core reads each once per startup epoch after the startup readback, disarmed, one upload per readback tick, and journals 'EtherCAT startup observe axis=... key=... value=...'; reads never write and never gate config_verified_mask. Prevents measuring drive-held tuning values with ethercat upload competing with rt-core for the mailbox.
axes.robot_joint_doc: Unverified example. Unit: robot joint token. Allowed: exactly one name in the pinned robot definition, with no duplicate selected joints. Default: required for robot-bound axes; omitted for flat axes. Prevents binding physical mechanics to the wrong bus axis.

collision_watchdog._unverified: unverified: bare-motor placeholders at drive ratio 1/1. Measured 2026-09-16 on the mini bench (docs/evidence/bench-minibench-2026-09-16): the 200-count limit tripped at 207 counts (0.57 degrees of motor shaft) after 10 cycles while the drive had produced 1 percent torque, so no bench move could start; 2000 counts (0.096 rad, just under the 0.1 rad following-error fault) and 500 raw torque units (50 percent) let the position loop build torque on an unloaded motor while the daemon following-error fault stays the ceiling. Re-measure once the motor moves.
